verdict.rationale: Slack ships a broad Web API, Events API, CLI, and MCP server covering messaging, channels, files, canvases, lists, and search (slack-docs-8, slack-docs-32, slack-docs-45, slack-docs-28, slack-docs-9), so most core workspace actions are API-accessible. However, concrete evidence shows real UI-only or restricted gaps: data export via API is gated behind Slack's approval and plan tier rather than freely available like the export UI implies (slack-comm-8), and rich UI-native features like Huddles (audio/video, screen share, huddle effects) have no documented API equivalent (slack-docs-18, slack-docs-33, slack-docs-24). Missing for 10: parity evidence for huddles/voice-video via API, unrestricted programmatic export matching UI export claims, and independent confirmation that all Workflow Builder no-code steps are fully API-scriptable.
